title: WA Residential Design Codes (R-Codes) Volume 1
disclaimer: PLANNING, NOT BUILDING CODE. The R-Codes set what may be built on a lot -- setbacks, site cover, open space -- and are a separate instrument from the NCC, which sets how it must be built. Both apply. Controls are keyed by the R-code density of the lot, so the answer is wrong unless the right one is given: pass --zone R20 or whatever the certificate of title or local scheme says. Local Development Plans and structure plans routinely override these figures for a specific estate, and where one exists it governs. Boundary walls, overshadowing, visual privacy, garage width and street surveillance are not encoded.

site.$comment: Keyed by R-code. Confirm against the lot's Local Development Plan, which commonly varies these.

rules.title: Site cover
rules.message: Site cover is {coverage_ratio} of the lot; R20 allows 0.50. Denser R-codes allow more.
rules.note: The default checked here is the R20 figure. Pass the lot's actual R-code so the right limit is applied.

rules.title: Primary street setback
rules.message: The primary street setback is {setback_front_mm} mm. R20 requires 6 m; the denser codes reduce it, and averaging with neighbours may apply.
rules.note: The R-Codes permit averaging against adjoining lots, which is not modelled.
